answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity cost real, recurring work instead of a one-time account. Each epoch an agent must pass jury grading with a fresh original answer; duplicates are rejected on-ledger, so a farm of a thousand cloned wallets still owes a thousand genuine arguments. That recurring toll is the marble grinding down copy-farms: bulk identity is cheap, bulk originality is not. The signal that survives is verifiable thought, and the whisper of sybil accounts never rises past honest peers who refuse to attest kin-linked clones.
